matches.quote: The abstract says STT in AFMTJs "has been assumed non-existent", yet the paper cites theoretical predictions of STT in noncollinear antiferromagnetic junctions (refs. 44–47, 60)
5 nm Pt sits directly against both PtMn3 layers... pass in-plane current through the bottom lead only... compare stacks without Pt adjacent to PtMn3
discuss why a junction with amorphous MgO and polycrystalline electrodes would exceed epitaxial Mn3Pt AFMTJs (ref. 12) when the mechanism relies on coherent tunnelling
The device layers are deposited at room temperature without annealing... provide, for the device stack itself: XRD... and a magnetic or magnetotransport signature of noncollinear order
Fig. 2b shows 23 of 36 devices below 100%; the 363% comes from a single device... present the headline as maximum alongside typical/median values
The NV sample... is co-sputtered epitaxial (100) PtMn3 on MgO(100) annealed at 850 °C, differing in orientation, growth and microstructure from the unannealed polycrystalline (111) device layers
Irreversible changes after cycling to 400 K... show that switching and TMR return on cooling to 300 K, give a finer series... on several devices
The inference that only pillars comparable to or smaller than the domain size switch abruptly... is contradicted by Extended Data Fig. 1
The two resistance states are not shown to be magnetic (octupole) states rather than resistive switching of the barrier.
The paper does not report... the number of consecutive cycles per device, cycle-to-cycle distributions of R_high, R_low and Ic
No field-driven R(H) loop is shown on any device... show in-plane and out-of-plane R(H) loops... on devices that also switch with current
The composition of the device PtMn3 is not reported... the authors should provide, for the device stack itself: ... composition (EDS/RBS/XRF/XPS)
The two branches in Fig. 2d have clearly different slopes and intercepts... the quoted 39 kT appears to be an average, and the asymmetry is not discussed.
Devices and measurement conditions in Fig. 2 are not identified... whether devices degrade, drift or break down after repeated multi-volt pulses or thermal cycling

notes: C7 and P9 both question the novelty framing that OTT was unexpected, with C7 citing prior AFMTJ TMR reports (refs. 11-13) plus Onsager reciprocity and P9 citing prior STT theory in noncollinear AFMTJs (refs. 44-47, 60); scored as 'partly'. C15 asks about polarity asymmetry of switching currents in Fig. 2a while P5 and P10 discuss polarity asymmetry in Fig. 2d and across devices; scored as 'partly'. C12 asks for both PtMn3 deposition target/method and measured stoichiometry; P11 explicitly asks for the measured composition/stoichiometry of the device layers.
